messages:
Sasha: Heads-up — Q2 forecast shows spike in embedding + rerank traffic around May 10-24 due to a marketing campaign. Need suggestions on pool strategy (separate pools? burst capacity?) :thinking_face:
Ria: Can you paste the demand curve? rough GPU-hours and qps targets help decide batching vs realtime split
Sasha: Quick numbers from analytics: baseline rerank qps=1.2k, embeddings batch jobs ~400 qps equivalent spread overnight. Peak rerank projected to 3.8k qps for ~36 hours. Estimated extra GPU-hours: ~18k over the 2-week window if we do no batching/optimization.
Michael: 18k sounds high — we should plan a hybrid: keep a dedicated low-latency pool for rerank (p95 target 120ms) and use batch pools for embeddings and low-priority rerank spillover. Separate pools reduce tail latency interference.
Anita: Agree. Propose: 1) rerank realtime pool sized for 2.5k sustained qps with burst to 4k for 48h (pre-warm nodes), 2) embeddings batch pool autoscale with pre-warmed spot instances for map-reduce jobs, 3) a small overflow pool for degraded rerank QoS at 300ms with cheaper quantized models.
Sasha: Nice. Quick calc: realtime pool (A100-equivalent) for 2.5k qps -> ~40 cards sustained, burst pad to 65 cards. overflow pool 10 cards, batch pool can flex to 80 cards overnight. Thoughts on GPU-hours booking?
Ria: If we reserve 65 cards for 48h that is 65*48 = 3120 card-hours. Batch 80*12 overnight *14 days = 13440 card-hours. overflow + baseline ~= 2500 card-hours. Total ~= 19000 card-hours, aligns with your 18k estimate after optimizations.
Michael: Cost tradeoff — reserved vs spot: reserve the realtime pool partially (commit 30 cards) and use on-demand/spot for burst. That avoids paying for 65 cards full time. Also consider packing efficiency: rerank runs small contexts — we can do increased batching during sub-1s windows to lower cost.
Anita: Region constraints: APAC demand is concentrated in same window; we should not cross-region route because latency SLOs. Suggest pre-warming 8-10 cards in APAC and rely on cross-region only for non-latency-sensitive batch.
Sasha: Good call. Also network / egress: rerank hits an external document store in GCP us-central; extra cross-region traffic could spike costs and hit network egress limits. Let's add egress estimate to the cost model.
infra-bot: CPU/GPU quota check: project/redwood-prod currently has available GPU quota = 120 cards in us-west, 20 cards in apac-1.
Ria: Given quota, we need to request a temporary quota bump for apac-1 to reach 40 cards for the peak. I'll file a quota request — ETA 48h approval if we put justification.
Michael: Simulation suggestion: run LoadSim with the actual qps trace + our SLOs. Example command:
```
./loadsim --trace traces/may_campaign_qps.json --model rerank-v1 --slo 120 --warmup 600 --duration 129600
```
Collect p50/p95/p99 and tail GPU utilization.
Sasha: I'll kick off that sim tonight against a staging cluster. Can someone own translating sim outputs into a provisioning request? We need exact card counts + recommended reserved commit levels.
Anita: I'll own the provisioning request (Anita). Ria, please attach the quota ticket link to the RFC.
Ria: Will do. Also adding a note: enable KV-prefix caching for rerank to cut token compute by ~12% — small win but helps cost.
Michael: Also consider quantized fallback model on overflow pool to keep correctness acceptable while saving ~30% GPU cycles. Add regression evals to the rollout.
Sasha: Summary action items: 1) Sasha -> run LoadSim and upload results (tonight), 2) Anita -> draft provisioning request & reserved commit proposal, 3) Ria -> file quota bump for apac-1 + attach to RFC, 4) Michael -> prepare cost delta for reserved vs spot for proposed pool mix, 5) infra-bot -> recheck quotas in 12h.
Anita: OK, I'll create the RFC doc and link the sim results. Meeting if sims show p95 > 140ms.
Sasha: thanks team :thumbsup:
